Environmental Engineering (PhD)
Environmental Engineering (PhD)

Request Info
The PhD in Environmental Engineering prepares researchers to define and solve original problems in water and environmental systems — treatment processes, surface water quality, hydrology, groundwater and contaminant transport, and the computational and data-driven methods these problems now demand. Doctoral students complete advanced coursework, pass a comprehensive examination covering a major and two minor subject areas, defend a research proposal, and produce and defend a dissertation of original scholarship.

Apply
Visit
At a Glance
53 credits of coursework: a comprehensive examination, a proposal defense, and a dissertation.
A dedicated environmental doctorate: required coursework in water and wastewater treatment, water resources engineering, hydrology and hydrogeology, and surface water quality.
Teaching and research assistantships: with stipend and tuition remission are available through the College.
Research in the EnviroAI Lab and the AnthroHydro Lab, in a city dense with federal environmental agencies and research sponsors.
Program Details
This is a research degree in environmental and water resources engineering. Coursework establishes command of the field, the comprehensive examination tests it, and everything after is original work conducted in continuous contact with the dissertation adviser.
Where the research happens
Doctoral work is conducted in the department’s environmental research laboratories. The EnviroAI Lab applies machine learning and data-driven modeling to environmental and water systems — inverse problems, uncertainty quantification, and the integration of physically based models with monitoring data. The AnthroHydro Lab studies human impacts on the water cycle. Students working at the intersection of environmental process modeling and computation often draw electives from data analysis, machine learning, optimization, and numerical methods with advisor approval.
Admission
Admission decisions are made by the College in consultation with the department, based on undergraduate and graduate transcripts, work experience and prior scholarly work, GRE scores, and at least three academic letters of recommendation. The minimum GPA for admission to doctoral study is 3.4. The GRE requirement may be waived where the College or department finds other evidence of a candidate’s proficiency, such as published work or professional experience. Non-native English speakers demonstrate proficiency through TOEFL scores or at least two years of study at an English-speaking institution.
Residence
Doctoral students enroll full-time — at least nine credit hours per semester — for a minimum of three semesters while completing coursework, then continue in extended residence until all requirements are met, registering for comprehensives or dissertation guidance unless granted a leave of absence.
Comprehensive examination
The comprehensive examination covers the candidate’s major area together with two minor subject areas related to the intended research. It may be taken after all required coursework is complete, or during the semester in which coursework will be finished; students register for ENGR 998A in the former case and ENGR 998B in the latter. A student who fails may sit the examination once more; a second failure ends eligibility to continue. Students advance to candidacy on completing the coursework and passing the examination.
Proposal, dissertation, and defense
The written proposal goes to every member of the doctoral committee at least two weeks before the proposal defense and must demonstrate a complete literature review, preliminary results already obtained, and a clear plan of research with specific tasks and expected outcomes. The dissertation must present original research giving evidence of excellent, significant, and original scholarship as established by external peer review, and must be approved by the directing professor and the dissertation committee. The final defense is administered by the full committee — at least three faculty members in addition to the chair and a College-assigned secretary — and is primarily on the dissertation. After advancing to candidacy, students register for at least one dissertation guidance course (ENGR 996) each semester and must complete all requirements within five years.
Curriculum
The Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Engineering requires 53 credits of coursework in addition to the comprehensive examination, proposal defense, and dissertation.
Coursework requirement (53 credits)
Three common core courses — 9 credits
Four required environmental engineering courses — 12 credits
Area electives — at least 32 credits (up to two ENGR 993 Directed Study courses, 6 credits total)
ENGR 998A or ENGR 998B in the semester of the comprehensive examination
ENGR 996 Dissertation Guidance every semester after advancement to candidacy
Courses and Electives
Common Core Courses
Doctoral students complete three of the following five common core courses:
ENGR 516 — Computational Methods in Engineering
ENGR 520 / ENGR 521 — Mathematical Analysis for Graduate Students / Partial Differential Equations
CEE / CMGT 575 — Introduction to Systems Analysis
CMGT 547 — Engineering Economics
ENGR 518 — Experimental Methods in Engineering
Additional core courses beyond the required number may be counted as area electives.
Required Environmental Engineering Courses
If a required course is not offered during a student’s period of study, another 500-level course may be substituted with the permission of the academic advisor or the graduate advising coordinator.
CEE 597 Water and Wastewater Treatment Engineering (alternating semesters)
CEE 526 Introduction to Finite Elements or CEE 565 Water Resources Engineering (Fall)
CEE 563 Applied Hydrology (Fall) or CEE 591 Hydrogeology (alternating semesters)
CEE 564 Surface Water Quality (alternating semesters) or CEE 511 Geographical Information Systems
Suggested Area Electives
The remaining credits are area electives selected in consultation with the academic advisor. The list below is a suggestion, not an exhaustive catalog; coursework in data analysis, machine learning, optimization, and numerical methods is frequently approved for students working on modeling problems.
CEE 538 Introduction to Environmental Engineering
CEE 571 Solid Waste Management
CEE 574 Environmental Processes
ME 529 Environmental Protection for Energy Systems
ME 550 Combustion and Waste Management
ARPL 531 Introduction to Sustainability
ARPL 538 LEED Lab: Sustainable Campus Building Assessment
ARPL 539 Topics in Construction and Environment
Transfer credit
Up to 24 credits from a master’s program completed elsewhere, or up to 30 credits from a master’s program completed at Catholic University, may be applied toward the doctoral coursework requirement.
FAQs
How is this different from the PhD in Civil Engineering?
The PhD in Environmental Engineering is a separate degree focused entirely on environmental and water resources engineering; within the PhD in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering and Water Resource Management is one of five areas of specialization. The required courses overlap, but the credential and the orientation of the elective pool differ. Discuss the choice with your prospective advisor — it usually turns on how you want the degree titled and how broadly you want to range.
How long does it take?
It depends on transfer credit and research progress. Students entering with a master’s may transfer up to 24 credits (30 if earned at Catholic University). After advancement to candidacy, all requirements must be completed within five years.
Is funding available?
Yes — teaching and research assistantships carrying a stipend and tuition remission are available through the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing. Contact the department and submit the College’s graduate TA/RA application materials.
Do I need an environmental engineering background?
Not necessarily. Applicants come from environmental, civil, chemical, and mechanical engineering as well as from the physical sciences. Admission is based on transcripts, prior scholarly work and experience, GRE scores, and at least three academic letters of recommendation, with a minimum GPA of 3.4; your advisor will identify any preparatory coursework.
Is the GRE required?
Yes for doctoral applicants, and scores are necessary for most university scholarships. The requirement may be waived where the College or department finds other evidence of proficiency, such as published work or substantial professional experience.
